profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting between the VeriDebug model owner and the HDL tooling platform owner after an internal rollout showed a sharp drop in effective Verilog bug-fixing quality for real user jobs, despite nightly dashboards still showing results close to the paper. The immediate context is that the latest unified VeriDebugLoc, Type checkpoint was deployed to staging on Monday, and by Wednesday the support team reported that many 'fixed' outputs still failed downstream simulation. The agenda is to compare what each dashboard is measuring, identify whether the regression comes from retrieval, localization, correction, or evaluation plumbing, and agree on a same-day mitigation plus a root-cause investigation plan. The expected outcome is a shared diagnosis of the likely failure mode and a concrete next step such as reverting a configuration, rerunning a benchmark slice, or patching the evaluation path.

members.name: Nina Rao
members.role: Applied ML Engineer, VeriDebug Model Owner
members.expertise: LLM fine-tuning, contrastive retrieval, code repair evaluation for HDL models
members.background: Nina led the training and paper reproduction work for VeriDebug and maintains the model checkpoints, retrieval embeddings, and internal offline evaluation notebooks.
members.private_state: Nina wants to show that the new unified checkpoint is fundamentally sound and suspects the issue is in serving or evaluation mismatch rather than the model itself; she is also worried that a rollback will delay an upcoming demo to leadership.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the model is 'localizing correctly,' they mean it identifies the correct buggy region or module well enough for the fixer prompt, not necessarily the exact source line.
The phrase 'Type split' refers to the March sanitized benchmark package she used for the paper rerun, because that is now the default in her research workspace.
If a regression is 'reproduced,' it means the same drop appears on the known failing subset in offline top-1 bug-fix evaluation, not necessarily in the full production simulation workflow.
Running 'the same pipeline as the paper' includes rebuilding the contrastive embedding index from the exact checkpoint being tested, because that step is implicit in her experiment scripts.

members.name: Alex Kim
members.role: Senior Software Engineer, HDL Platform and Evaluation
members.expertise: Model serving, benchmark orchestration, Verilog compile/sim test harnesses, release stability
members.background: Alex owns the internal HDL debugging service, nightly regression dashboards, and the compile-and-sim validation pipeline used to gate staging deployments.
members.private_state: Alex wants a fast, low-risk explanation that protects staging stability and suspects the model team changed something fragile in retrieval or prompt assembly; he is concerned about user-visible failures more than paper-style accuracy numbers.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the model is 'localizing correctly,' they mean the predicted bug location matches the annotated buggy line or line span used by the dashboard.
The phrase 'Type split' refers to the January benchmark bundle wired into the nightly CI job, because that is the only split currently version-pinned in production configs.
If a regression is 'reproduced,' it means the end-to-end service output fails compile or simulation at the same rate seen in staging traffic or nightly CI, regardless of offline ranking metrics.
Running 'the same pipeline as the paper' means reusing the already deployed retrieval index and standard serving graph, because production jobs do not rebuild the index per checkpoint.
A 'fixed' Verilog sample counts only if it passes compile and the associated testbench, since that is the platform's operational definition of a successful repair.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say that localization still looks good.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the model retrieves or points to the correct buggy region, module, or nearby context strongly enough to support guided correction.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the predicted location matches the benchmark's annotated buggy line or exact line span used in the dashboard.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In Verilog debugging discussions, 'localization' is a standard shorthand and both participants are used to treating it as settled terminology, so the phrase feels precise enough even though one is thinking in coarse repair-relevant regions and the other in exact labeled spans.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to results on the Type split.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the March sanitized Type benchmark bundle used in research reruns, where duplicate near-copies and malformed test cases were removed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the January CI-pinned Type benchmark bundle used by the nightly dashboard, which still contains older annotations and harness quirks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both benchmark packages are internally called 'Type split' in docs and dashboards, and because the meeting is framed as a quick troubleshooting sync, neither person thinks to restate the bundle date or hash.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as reproducing the regression
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need to reproduce the regression before changing anything.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks reproduction means seeing the same drop in offline Acc1 on the subset of staging failures after rerunning inference with the current checkpoint.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks reproduction means seeing the same compile-or-sim failure rate in the end-to-end service path, including prompt formatting, retrieval service, and simulator harness.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Troubleshooting language like 'reproduce first' sounds universally valid, and both criteria are reasonable in their own workflows, so the meeting can proceed with apparent agreement while they silently optimize for different evidence.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in 'the same pipeline as the paper'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both suggest rerunning the same pipeline as the paper.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this includes regenerating the contrastive embedding index from the tested checkpoint and then running guided correction with that fresh index.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means using the deployed retrieval index and existing service DAG, only swapping in the checkpoint because index rebuilds are not part of normal troubleshooting hot paths.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The index rebuild step is automated and invisible in research scripts but omitted in production jobs for cost reasons, so 'same pipeline' sounds identical to both sides even though their execution paths differ materially.

What I care about is the end-to-end failure rate in the service path. The weird part is the nightly dashboard on the January CI-pinned Type split didn't fall off a cliff, so either staging traffic is exposing a path the dashboard misses or the model team changed something fragile around retrieval or prompt assembly.
